answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring capital commitment as an inlet for consensus participation. By tethering influence to asset ownership, the protocol forces an attacker to purchase a sparrow of the total circulating supply to subvert the network. This economic barrier transforms a simple identity forgery into a cost-prohibitive sonnet of fiscal loss, ensuring that malicious actors cannot scale virtual identities without incurring massive, unavoidable financial penalties.
